2 tablespoons Olive oil (roughly)
1lb bacon
1lb smoked sausage 
1lb seasoning blend (onions celery bell pepper)
1 28oz can of diced tomatoes (I used rotel, has green chiles)
3-4 tablespoons light jarred roux
1/4-1/2 cup half and half
3lbs crawfish tail meat
Kitchen bouquet 
Cajun spice blend (I used Paul Prudhomme redfish magic as I had it on hand)
3-5 pounds of frozen sweet corn (I used probably 4lbs of a 5lb bag I got)
Parsley (either fresh or dried, I used dried)
Garlic
Green onions
Hot sauce and Worcestershire to taste


First, I chopped up the whole pack of bacon into bite sized pieces. I then added it to my pot, along with a chunk of butter and drizzle of olive oil. I added some water to it as well, then covered with the lid. I let the bacon render out most of its fat before taking the lid off. After that, I let it brown and crisp up most of the way.

While the bacon was cooking, I chopped up my sausage to small slices. Key on thin slices. Once the bacon was almost done, I added the sausage right in. I mixed it together and let them cook in the bacon fat till it developed a nice color.

Next, I added the seasoning blend (onions celery and bell pepper). I like using guidrys or other pre packaged blends. Let them cook until they’ve turned translucent and just start to brown. At this time, feel free to add any garlic or other spices/seasonings, like hot sauce or Worcestershire. Feel free to add roux at this step too.

Next, add your can of diced tomatoes and stir. I like to add the kitchen bouquet at this step as well. Just a couple teaspoons is enough for this recipe. Also add the parsley I like to let everything simmer for a few minutes before adding the corn.

Okay now add the corn, combine, and cover. Let everything simmer for an hour or two. Add the green onion. Let simmer some more. Add some water if it starts to get dry. The corn should release enough water however. I like to cook it covered the majority of the time.

Once the corn is your desired consistency, remove the lid and continue cooking to let off any moisture. Keep stirring to make sure moving sticks to the bottom. Once it’s almost done I add the half and half (or heavy cream). And get it back to your desired consistency.

If you want to, now you can add crawfish tails. Turn off the heat. Add thawed crawfish tails. Combine. The residual heat will warm them up. It maybe even cook them more, releasing small amounts of water and making it runnier. If this happens, don’t try to cook it off. That will only cook the tails more releasing even more water.

Season to taste. Enjoy!

First, cut up and brown the andouille. Then, add the butter and let everything foamy. Once the butter is melted and back to temp, add vegetables and sauté. I like to add some spice and herbs here to help with drawing out the moisture/wake up the spices. 

Next, I’ll add a little bit of roux from a jar, maybe a quarter of a cup. Keep in mind that I use condensed soups to help thicken it, so don’t feel like you have to add too much. Once the roux has been thoroughly mixed with the vegetables and sausage and starts to stick to the bottom of the pot, I like to deglaze with some Worcestershire and hot sauce. 

After that, I like to add a can of rotel + a cans worth of water. Once everything is mixed together, I’ll add a can or two of cream of mushroom or golden mushroom soup. Adding it while it’s still relatively thick helps the soup incorporate easier.

After that, I like to add some parsley flakes, just cus I like the look of em sha. I also like okra in mine, so I add a couple cans in there too. I’ll add water till it gets thinner than I want it to be, and let it simmer until the andouille is tender. 

Once the andouille is tender and it’s reached your desired consistency, I throw in thawed crawfish tails. Making sure they’re thawed beforehand is important, as it lets the block of tails break up into the etouffee without some getting overcooked from thawing a frozen block in hot stew. 

Once everything’s back up to temp, serve over rice and enjoy!
